offences.quote: Failure to reference AI use correctly is malpractice.
Misuse of AI tools in relation to qualification assessments at any time constitutes malpractice
Copying or paraphrasing sections of AI-generated content so that the work submitted for assessment is no longer the student’s own.
Making a false declaration of authenticity in relation to the authorship of controlled assessments, coursework or the contents of a portfolio.
Using AI to complete parts of the assessment so that the work does not reflect the student’s own work, analysis, evaluation or calculations.
Plagiarism: unacknowledged copying from published sources or incomplete referencing.
Failing to abide by the conditions of supervision designed to maintain the security ofthe examinations or assessments.
Collusion: working collaboratively with other learners, beyond what is permitted.
Impersonation: pretending to be someone else, arranging for another person to take one’s place in an examination or an assessment.

detection.quote: teacher professional judgement and familiarity with students’ typical writing style and ability

process.quote: it will conduct an investigation in a form commensurate with the nature of the assessment malpractice and maladministration allegation.
Should it be determined that a full investigation is necessary it shall be conducted by an independent investigation officer appointed by the College Principal .
During the investigation the college will give the individual the opportunity to respond to all the allegations made.
Subject to agreement it may be appropriate for a member of staff from the awarding organisation to give evidence at any hearing called as part of the investigation.
The individual(s) concerned has/have the right to appeal against any decision(s) or sanction(s) imposed.
An appeal must be made in writing to the College Principal within 30 working days from receipt of the written notification of the reported incident.
All stages of the investigation shall be documented by the investigating officer leading the investigation.

outcomes.quote: The learner is issued with a warning that if the offence is repeated within a set period oftime, further specified sanctions will be applied.

The learner loses all the marks gained for a discrete section of the work.
The learner loses all the marks gained for a unit.
The learner could be barred from entering for one or more examinations for a set period oftime.
make retake the component(s), unit(s), or qualification(s) affectedin the next examination series or assessment opportunity.

outcomes.quote: Misuse of AI tools in relation to qualification assessments at any time constitutes malpractice and in accordance with JCQ regulations may attract severe sanctions.

definitions.quote: AI misuse is where a student has used one or more AI tools but has not appropriately acknowledged this use and has submitted work for assessment which is not their own.
Plagiarism: unacknowledged copying from published sources or incomplete referencing.
Collusion: working collaboratively with other learners, beyond what is permitted.
Impersonation: pretending to be someone else, arranging for another person to take one’s place in an examination or an assessment.
